Explanation: The large stellar association cataloged as NGC 206 is nestled within the dusty arms of the neighboring Andromeda galaxy along with the galaxy's pinkish star-forming regions. Also known as M31, the spiral galaxy is a mere 2.5 million light-years away.

NGC 206 is found at the center of this sharp and detailed close-up of the southwestern extent of Andromeda's disk. The bright, blue stars of NGC 206 indicate its youth. In fact, its youngest massive stars are less than 10 million years old.

Much larger than the open or galactic clusters of young stars in the disk of our Milky Way galaxy, NGC 206 spans about 4,000 light-years. That's comparable in size to the giant stellar nurseries NGC 604 in nearby spiral M33 and the Tarantula Nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud.

articles.title: A Global Rebound for Mangroves
articles.summary: After decades of decline, this ecologically significant type of forest is making a comeback. Scientists began using satellites to map mangrove forests in the 1970s after the launch of the first Landsat satellite.
articles.summary_short: After decades of decline, this ecologically significant type of forest is making a comeback. Scientists began using satellites to map mangrove forests in the 1970s after the launch of the first Landsat satellite.
articles.summary_long:
After decades of decline, this ecologically significant type of forest is making a comeback. Scientists began using satellites to map mangrove forests in the 1970s after the launch of the first Landsat satellite. A global rebound began around 2010, the scientists found, led by the expansion of mangrove forests in Asia, Australia, and South America.

They tallied losses of nearly 3,000 square kilometers (1,200 square miles) between 1984 and 2010, followed by an unexpected increase of nearly 2,000 square kilometers (770 square miles) of mangroves after 2010. They also found that many of today's mangrove forests have denser, more closed canopies than they did in 2010, a sign of healthier, less degraded forests, particularly in South America. The pair of Landsat images above shows expansion of mangrove forests in Palaw Township in Burma's Myeik District—an area that has seen both significant regeneration of degraded mangrove forests and the spread of trees into new areas since 2010.

Since then, the country's mangrove area has grown about 10 percent. Mangrove trees are relatively small—averaging about 13 meters (43 feet)—but mighty from an ecological perspective, with mangrove ecosystems storing up to four times as much carbon as taller inland tropical forests. Substantial mangrove losses in the Niger Delta, for instance, have reduced the total mangrove area in West and Central Africa since 2010.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman
articles.summary: Gravitational lensing, first predicted by Albert Einstein, occurs when the gravity of a massive foreground object, such as a galaxy or cluster of galaxies, bends, warps, and magnifies the light from a more distant background object. Panel I shows a quadruply lensed galaxy, in which the background galaxy is replicated four times, appearing as smeared dots around the foreground galaxy.
articles.summary_short: Gravitational lensing, first predicted by Albert Einstein, occurs when the gravity of a massive foreground object, such as a galaxy or cluster of galaxies, bends, warps, and magnifies the light from a more distant background object. Panel I shows a quadruply lensed galaxy, in which the background galaxy is replicated four times, appearing as smeared dots around the foreground galaxy.
articles.summary_long:
A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Gravitational lensing, first predicted by Albert Einstein, occurs when the gravity of a massive foreground object, such as a galaxy or cluster of galaxies, bends, warps, and magnifies the light from a more distant background object. The lenses in this image formed from the precise alignment of a distant background galaxy with the mass of a foreground galaxy, creating distorted and magnified images of the background galaxy that appear as arcs around the foreground galaxy.

Panel A is an example of an arc-counterarc configuration, in which the lensed background galaxy appears as a duplicated pair of arcs. The lensed galaxy is being magnified by a pair of foreground galaxies whose combined mass bends the light of the background galaxy around them. Panel F is an Einstein Ring, in which the alignment of the background galaxy and approximately spherical mass of the foreground lens are so perfectly situated that the lensed galaxy almost fully encircles the foreground galaxy.

Panel I shows a quadruply lensed galaxy, in which the background galaxy is replicated four times, appearing as smeared dots around the foreground galaxy. Lensed images of background galaxies only occur when the mass density of the foreground galaxy reaches a critical point. Panel D’s foreground galaxy has a visible dust lane, which is rare in a lensing galaxy and the kind of detail that Hubble’s sharp, visible-light vision excels at revealing.

articles.title: How Show Jumping Vets Use Thermal Cameras to Catch Horse Abuse
articles.summary: The FEI's veterinary rulebook contains one number that decides nothing at all. Two identical stud walls in the same frame, one cold and one not.
articles.summary_short: The FEI's veterinary rulebook contains one number that decides nothing at all. Two identical stud walls in the same frame, one cold and one not.
articles.summary_long:
The FEI's veterinary rulebook contains one number that decides nothing at all. A temperature difference of more than two degrees Celsius between a horse's left and right lower limbs counts as a significant thermographic finding, and a significant thermographic finding eliminates nobody, fines nobody, and never becomes the result of record. Two examining veterinarians appointed by the FEI Veterinary Department run the exam.

Article 1047.6 then defines what counts as a significant thermographic finding, and there are exactly two of them: "A temperature difference between collateral limbs exceeding two degrees Celsius," and a localized or generalized region of high or low temperature in one or more limbs. These are two different lists, and the camera cannot generate an entry on the second one. Two degrees between one leg and the other, in the same frame, under the same sky, with the same assumed emissivity, is a comparison in which most of a camera's systematic error simply cancels.

At rest, the two limbs were indistinguishable, 15.3 °C under each. Two identical stud walls in the same frame, one cold and one not. Two sides of the same roof, shot in the same minute from the same distance.

Tracing paper on the back of the tank with flash pushed through it produced a central ball of glow instead of the clean white background Taylor wanted, so he switched to two Elinchrom 600 heads lighting a white wall behind the tank.

One Nissin fires down through the water's surface at 1/128 power, and as ripples form, it throws the same dappled light you see on the bottom of a swimming pool across the labels. Two more shine through tracing paper on one side at quarter power to give the bottles shape, with the lens at f/16 for depth of field and a single transmitter triggering one flash while the rest fire on their optical slaves. The same logic runs through the whole setup: fix every variable you can, so the only thing left to chance is the one element you want to be unpredictable.

Glue holds the bottles, flags and white surfaces control the light, and the water gets to be wild. A tank creates problems a tabletop never does. Taylor ends with two frames to build from.

articles.title: Why the Most Memorable Photos Ask a Question They Never Answer
articles.summary: You come home from a trip with hundreds of sharp, well-exposed frames of towers, smiling friends, and pretty streets, and almost none of them hold a stranger's attention for more than a second. The photos you remember from books and exhibitions share one trait that has little to do with gear or settings, and you can learn to build it into your own work.
articles.summary_short: You come home from a trip with hundreds of sharp, well-exposed frames of towers, smiling friends, and pretty streets, and almost none of them hold a stranger's attention for more than a second. The photos you remember from books and exhibitions share one trait that has little to do with gear or settings, and you can learn to build it into your own work.
articles.summary_long:
You come home from a trip with hundreds of sharp, well-exposed frames of towers, smiling friends, and pretty streets, and almost none of them hold a stranger's attention for more than a second. The photos you remember from books and exhibitions share one trait that has little to do with gear or settings, and you can learn to build it into your own work. The images Kent admires work differently, and he points to Sam Stone, an Instagram photographer he calls a master of this, whose images nearly all leave you wondering.

What is that person angry at, and what are they staring at just outside the frame? Information gap theory, laid out in a 1994 paper by the behavioral economist George Loewenstein, describes curiosity as the feeling that arises when you notice a gap between what you know and what you want to know. Before you press the shutter, decide what the frame will answer and what it will hold back.

When you arrive somewhere new, it's tempting to shoot the whole tower, the whole square, the whole vista. There was never anything in it, and that's the point: what sits outside the frame matters far less than what the frame makes the viewer imagine. If you want to see the idea at work, he suggests spending some time in a local photo book shop, where you'll find it in most of the pictures on the shelves.

Leica ‘s Noctilux family has spent six decades doing both, and the company is marking the anniversary with a 240 page book documenting the technology, photographers, and designs behind its famously fast lenses.

Simply titled Noctilux , the hardcover traces the lens family’s development from its introduction in 1966 to the latest 35mm model. Beyond the individual lenses, the book explores the development of aspherical optics and how manufacturing techniques evolved over the decades. Peter Karbe, the company’s Senior Managing Expert in Optics, discusses the history of aspherical lenses, while Dietmar Stuible, Head of Optics Development since 2021, explains the mechanical design of M lenses .

Stuible describes the significance of the lens family: “Every Noctilux in the history of the lens family has represented a technological milestone, taking lens development to a new level.” The book also looks beyond specifications and manufacturing history. The volume also includes a gallery of special editions and one of a kind lenses, along with an index covering Leica M lenses throughout the company’s history. For photographers interested in the history of lens design, this is a chance to explore six decades of optical experimentation without having to track down six decades of glass.

Photographers sharing their work online have another thing to worry about beyond unauthorized reposts: their images potentially becoming training material for generative AI . In a message to photographers , CEO Eric Wittman said the revised Creator Content Standards clarify how VSCO handles user content and distinguish between the AI tools it uses to support photographers and systems designed to generate new images or videos.

Wittman said VSCO does not use public or private user content to train generative AI models. The company also says its external AI providers have agreed not to use content submitted through VSCO services to train generative AI models. VSCO says it uses machine learning and non-generative AI across its platform to help photographers find work , discover people, edit images, and use its services.

VSCO says it wants to continue using AI to improve tools and services for photographers while keeping their submitted content out of generative AI training. VSCO’s announcement comes amid growing debate over how creative work is used to develop generative AI systems. Wittman framed the policy update as part of VSCO’s commitment to photographers, saying the company should help creators make a living from their work rather than treat their images as material for systems that generate new content.

La batterie LP-E17, la même que celle de l’EOS R8, est annoncée pour 340 vues à l’écran et 220 au viseur (CIPA). Le Canon EOS R8 Mark II n’a qu’un emplacement SD UHS-II , placé sur le côté : prévoyez une carte de rechange et une sauvegarde régulière, sur le smartphone, un SSD ou image.canon .

Les utilisateurs d’EOS RP ou d’EOS R8 y trouveront la stabilisation et le joystick qui leur manquaient. Pour voyager léger, le Canon EOS R8 Mark II couvre l’essentiel . articles.title: How Sky Glabush Conjures Atmospheric Landscapes in Sand and Oil Paint
articles.summary: Looking at the serene paintings that emerge from Sky Glabush ’ s studio, it’s easy to feel a soft breeze sliding off bare summer shoulders or hear the crunch of leaves underfoot, their parched fibers reverberating across the autumn landscape. Transportive and atmospherically charged, the landscapes harness the allure of texture to draw the viewer in and invite them to stay a while.
articles.summary_short: Looking at the serene paintings that emerge from Sky Glabush ’ s studio, it’s easy to feel a soft breeze sliding off bare summer shoulders or hear the crunch of leaves underfoot, their parched fibers reverberating across the autumn landscape. Transportive and atmospherically charged, the landscapes harness the allure of texture to draw the viewer in and invite them to stay a while.
articles.summary_long:
Looking at the serene paintings that emerge from Sky Glabush ’ s studio, it’s easy to feel a soft breeze sliding off bare summer shoulders or hear the crunch of leaves underfoot, their parched fibers reverberating across the autumn landscape. Transportive and atmospherically charged, the landscapes harness the allure of texture to draw the viewer in and invite them to stay a while. Glabush typically utilizes limited palettes that adhere to just one or two color families.

Originally, the idea of combining materials emerged because the artist wanted, he says, to “obliterate the image… But I realized it didn’t destroy the image. So it gave me the freedom of deciding what I wanted to hold on to or what I wanted to erase.” Adding and removing has since become integral to Glabush’s practice, which involves adding thin stains of paint and turpentine to the point of the painting becoming relief-like. Sometimes a grid and others a radial arrangement, the foundational patterns inform each resulting layer.

Each painting often goes through several iterations of colour before deciding on a direction.” Although he’s worked with other materials in the past and has particularly enjoyed carving, the conventions and limitations of painting always drew him back. “That period of experimentation with sculpture allowed me to treat my paintings in a more physically robust and experimental way. But even during my most experimental period, I saw myself as a painter and wanted to find a way to express myself within that language,” he tells Colossal.

articles.title: Peter Morris Architects’ Pastel Pink ‘Cloud House’ Billows in Northwest London
articles.summary: A confection of arches and windows has emerged in the Gospel Oak neighborhood of Camden in northwest London, thanks to Peter Morris Architects and a unique collaborative ownership approach. “The Cloud House,” which actually comprises two side-by-side townhomes, practically froths from its foundations.
articles.summary_short: A confection of arches and windows has emerged in the Gospel Oak neighborhood of Camden in northwest London, thanks to Peter Morris Architects and a unique collaborative ownership approach. “The Cloud House,” which actually comprises two side-by-side townhomes, practically froths from its foundations.
articles.summary_long:
A confection of arches and windows has emerged in the Gospel Oak neighborhood of Camden in northwest London, thanks to Peter Morris Architects and a unique collaborative ownership approach. “The Cloud House,” which actually comprises two side-by-side townhomes, practically froths from its foundations. One side is occupied by the architect himself along with his partner, Emily, while the other half is owned by a resident who embraced the stylistic potential of the project and agreed to the exterior design and the same contractor.

Ten years in the making, “The Cloud House” is a playful response to its eclectic neighboring architecture, from the quirky Victorian church of St. Martin’s to a school next door that has a stone exterior mimicking a castle. Morris conceived of a bright, whimsical design with pink walls, robin’s egg-blue window frames and doors, and arched details in relief made from a dense recyclable polystyrene that mirrors the arches of the church across the street.

articles.summary_long:
OpenAI étoffe sa plateforme de cybersécurité Daybreak avec deux solutions reposant sur des agents d’intelligence artificielle. Présentés le 12 novembre 2026, Daybreak Red Team et Daybreak Defense Factory visent respectivement à automatiser les tests d’intrusion et à accélérer la préparation des correctifs. OpenAI poursuit le développement de son offre de cybersécurité Daybreak, lancée en mai 2026.

Avec ces deux nouveaux produits destinés aux équipes de sécurité applicative, Daybreak franchit une nouvelle étape. Le premier, Daybreak Red Team, mobilise des agents d’IA pour conduire des tests d’intrusion sur des applications web. Malgré la proximité des noms, il ne doit pas être confondu avec Daybreak Red, l’un des deux niveaux d’accès aux modèles cyber d’OpenAI.

Le second, Daybreak Defense Factory, intervient dans l’analyse des vulnérabilités et la préparation des correctifs. Avec Daybreak Defense Factory, OpenAI cherche à réduire le volume de vulnérabilités en attente de traitement. Les agents peuvent exploiter les résultats des outils de sécurité existants ainsi que les vulnérabilités confirmées par Daybreak Red Team.

articles.title: Scotland’s Flow Country
articles.summary: Blanket bogs in the Scottish Highlands store vast amounts of carbon. The bogs store tremendous quantities of carbon .
articles.summary_short: Blanket bogs in the Scottish Highlands store vast amounts of carbon. The bogs store tremendous quantities of carbon .
articles.summary_long:
Blanket bogs in the Scottish Highlands store vast amounts of carbon. Compared to ecosystems in many other parts of the world, the blanket bogs of the Flow Country in northern Scotland are unassuming—soggy, treeless landscapes dominated by hummocky mosses, grasses, and heathers. The bogs store tremendous quantities of carbon .

Instead, partially decayed plant matter accumulates into thick layers of spongy, crumbly, carbon-rich material called peat . These types of bogs cover just 120,000 square kilometers (46,000 square miles) globally, less than one-tenth of one percent of Earth’s land surface. The peat bogs of northern Scotland, home to more than 30 species of sphagnum moss , are spread across some 1,900 square kilometers (730 square miles) of the country’s Highlands region.

While forests store most of their carbon in living trees—which eventually release it back into the atmosphere when they burn or die—peat bogs often store carbon for many thousands of years. Overall, scientists estimate that all of the world’s peatlands cover just 3 percent of Earth’s land surface but store more than 600 gigatons of carbon—about twice as much as all the world’s forests combined. You use a red headlamp when you're walking around. But if there are other astro-landscape photographers nearby, you're likely ruining their shots. Most of us were taught that red light is the night photographer's best friend.

If you use a red light, your eyes stay more adapted to the dark. Your camera sensor records red light very well. Red light also doesn't stay where you point it.

When we begin night photography workshops, we ask that no one use red headlamps or red lights when we are photographing out in the field. If there are other photographers nearby, I would encourage you not to use red headlamps or other red lights unless you know that it won't cause an issue with them. And white light does wreck adaptation more readily than red light.

Zoom a publié des correctifs pour deux vulnérabilités affectant Workplace sous Windows, dont une faille critique d’élévation de privilèges notée 9,6 sur l’échelle CVSS. Référencées CVE-2026-108186 et CVE-2026-108187, elles pourraient permettre à un attaquant non authentifié d’obtenir des privilèges supplémentaires à distance, à condition que l’utilisateur interagisse. Zoom renforce la sécurité de son application collaborative Workplace pour Windows.

Son exploitation nécessite toutefois une interaction de l’utilisateur, conformément au vecteur CVSS publié par Zoom. Le deuxième correctif concerne CVE-2026-108187, une faille de gravité élevée, évaluée à 8,1 sur l’échelle CVSS. Les versions de Zoom Workplace pour Windows antérieures à la 7.1.5 sont concernées.

Elle affectait Zoom Workplace pour Windows dans les versions antérieures à 7.0.0, ainsi que certaines versions du client VDI pour Windows. Leur exploitation nécessite notamment une interaction de l’utilisateur, contrairement à la faille corrigée en juillet. Compte tenu de la gravité de CVE-2026-108186, une mise à jour rapide vers Zoom Workplace 7.1.8 ou une version ultérieure est recommandée.

Les chercheurs ont identifié 43 601 noms d’applications associés au domaine grok.me, utilisé pour leur publication.

Les adresses attribuées aux applications comportent généralement quatre mots aléatoires. Toutes les applications accessibles ne contenaient pas des données confidentielles. Les chercheurs estiment qu’entre 650 et 800 applications contenaient des données privées.

articles.summary_long:
There's a strange gamma-ray emitter in the Large Magellanic Cloud that has astronomers stumped about its source. It lies within the ashes left behind by a supernova that created a compact object that's part of the system. It consists of a giant O-type star and a compact object that could be explained by the existence of a black hole or a neutron star.

âWe discovered a gigantic molecular jet,â said Fukui. They actually consist of two objects: a stellar-mass black hole or neutron star coupled with a companion star. It's a fairly energetic interaction that leads to X-ray and gamma-ray emissions.

The discovery of the newly found "cold" jet strongly suggests that the compact object could be a stellar-mass black hole or neutron star that draws in material from its companion to form an accretion disk. Object LMC P3 was first discovered in 2016 thanks to its very strong gamma-ray emissions. Then, the FERMI telescope observed it and found a 10.3-day period in gamma-ray emissions from the object.

articles.summary_long:
Advances in computing and astronomy have led to increasingly complex attempts to chart the large-scale structure of the Universe. For the past decade, scientists have been working to map one aspect in particular to see whether it matches observations of the cosmic web: cosmic hydrogen. For the past decade, scientists with the MeerKLASS Collaboration have been trying to measure how neutral hydrogen "clumps" in the distant Universe.

In a study published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS), the team announced the first direct measurement of the large-scale structure of cosmic hydrogen. The MeerKLASS (MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey) Collaboration is an international group of astronomers conducting cosmological surveys using the MeerKAT radio telescope. Their survey relies on a technique known as HI intensity (or 21-cm intensity) mapping to detect the combined emissions of galaxies within large segments of the sky.

Their results showed that cosmic hydrogen mirrors the large-scale structure of the cosmic web, advancing a technique that could transform how cosmologists map the Universe. For more information, check out his website . For more information, check out his website .

articles.title: Why Aging Stars Suffer A Sudden Luminosity Dip
articles.summary: From a naked eye perspective, stars are stable and predictable. This work ties the RGB luminosity bump to this boundary.
articles.summary_short: From a naked eye perspective, stars are stable and predictable. This work ties the RGB luminosity bump to this boundary.
articles.summary_long:
From a naked eye perspective, stars are stable and predictable. Their observations reveal the changes stars experience during their long lifetimes. As low-mass stars like the Sun exhaust their hydrogen supplies and evolve, they become Red Giant Branch (RGB) stars.

But for some reason, there's a brief and abrupt dip in their brightness known as the RGB luminosity bump . But what initiates the bump is still unexplained. In models, the bump appears at higher luminosities than the observed bump, meaning it appears later.

"To understand why the bump appears later in the models than in observations, the physics of the bump needs to be unravelled," Hekker writes. Stars, including our Sun, are layered, and RGB stars are no exception. This work ties the RGB luminosity bump to this boundary.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Don’t judge a galaxy by its size. Our home galaxy, the Milky Way , is about 100,000 light years across.

This huge expanse of space contains hundreds of billions of stars! The smallest galaxies, called dwarf galaxies , are about 1/10th the size of the Milky Way and only contain a few billion stars. They are also the most common type of galaxy in the whole universe.

Today’s image shows one such dwarf galaxy, NGC 4449 , captured by the Hubble Space Telescope . NGC 4449 and similar dwarf galaxies are missing more oxygen than models predict. Turns out these tiny galaxies may play a big role in spreading heavy elements — the building blocks of stars, planets, and life — throughout the universe!

“By themselves, double white dwarfs will emit gravitational waves at a nearly continuous frequency. For gravitational waves, the sidebands carry messages about the presence of a planet. articles.title: Amy Genser’s Elaborate Mulberry Paper Assemblages Undulate Like the Sea
articles.summary: Plumbing the rhythms of the ocean and marine life, Amy Genser creates undulating abstractions that evoke swells, currents, reefs, and the sea floor. Although reminiscent of the sea in many ways, Genser’s works defy instant recognition.
articles.summary_short: Plumbing the rhythms of the ocean and marine life, Amy Genser creates undulating abstractions that evoke swells, currents, reefs, and the sea floor. Although reminiscent of the sea in many ways, Genser’s works defy instant recognition.
articles.summary_long:
Plumbing the rhythms of the ocean and marine life, Amy Genser creates undulating abstractions that evoke swells, currents, reefs, and the sea floor. The artist composes elaborate wall works from rolled mulberry paper, acrylic, and wire in which patterns move and converge across swaths of blues and greens. Although reminiscent of the sea in many ways, Genser’s works defy instant recognition.

At first glance, they may appear topographical, as if a luminous, clear sea is being viewed from above. The rolling forms are redolent of waves but also perhaps the way corals cluster around rock formations. Then, details draw us nearer: bulbous forms with cavities resemble barnacles, and extended shapes could be tentacles.

The artist’s play on scale, texture, pattern, and depth draw us in and keep us guessing—not unlike the many enigmas of the ocean itself. And one recent project challenged Genser to work at a monumental scale. “Through layered textures, flowing forms, and rich colors, I brought to life a mythical underwater world shaped by movement, discovery, and transformation,” Genser says.

articles.summary_long:
Scality a annoncé le 10 novembre 2026 son entrée dans le programme CVE en tant qu’autorité de numérotation, ou CNA (CVE Numbering Authority). L’éditeur peut désormais attribuer directement des identifiants aux vulnérabilités de ses logiciels et publier les enregistrements associés. Scality rejoint le programme sous l’autorité racine, ou « Root », gérée par l’Agence de l’Union européenne pour la cybersécurité, l’ENISA.

Le périmètre de Scality couvre ses propres logiciels, notamment Scality RING, Scality ARTESCA et Scality ADI. Scality indique que ses clients avaient expressément demandé une couverture CVE de ses produits. Pour Anh Nguyen-Phuoc, responsable de la sécurité des systèmes d’information de Scality, ce dispositif répond aux attentes de clients opérant dans des environnements fortement réglementés.

Scality inscrit son statut de CNA dans une démarche plus large. L’entreprise indique disposer d’un système de management de la sécurité de l’information certifié ISO 27001. Jérôme Lecat, directeur général et cofondateur de Scality, présente cette participation au programme CVE comme une contribution à la souveraineté numérique européenne et à la transparence attendue par les clients publics et privés.

Siemens a annoncé le 10 novembre 2026 un accord pour acquérir Lauterbach, spécialiste allemand des outils de débogage et de traçage des logiciels embarqués. Le groupe entend renforcer son offre de conception électronique et permettre aux développeurs de tester ensemble les puces et leurs logiciels avant la fabrication des composants. Lauterbach doit rejoindre l’activité d’automatisation de la conception électronique de Siemens, connue sous le sigle EDA.

Cette branche, qui fournit des outils de conception et de vérification des puces, s’est notamment développée avec le rachat de Mentor Graphics en 2017. Fondée en 1979 par les frères Lothar et Stephan Lauterbach, l’entreprise est installée à Höhenkirchen, près de Munich. Lauterbach dispose également de bureaux au Royaume-Uni, en Italie, en France, en Tunisie, aux États-Unis, au Japon et en Chine.

Siemens prévoit d’associer ces technologies à ses solutions de vérification assistée par matériel. Siemens entend réduire les délais de développement et de commercialisation. Stephan Lauterbach et Thomas Ullmann poursuivront leurs activités au sein de Siemens après la clôture de l’opération.

Martian dust is a major hurdle for human missions to Mars. Like Moon dust, its fine size and electrostatically charged nature allow it to stick to spacesuits, metal, and just about any other surface they come into contact with. Dust storms are also common on Mars, ranging from small whirlwinds that happen daily to global dust storms that occur once every 3 Martian years (~5.5 Earth years) and envelop the entire planet.

In summary, the results showed that Martian dust may be less likely to be abrasive to equipment or harmful to astronaut health than lunar regolith. In addition, Martian dust can be exceptionally fine, with some ultrafine particles measuring as little as 100 nanometers (nm) in diameter. With Martian dust carrying perchlorates and other toxins, the health risk is magnified.

Each has advantages and disadvantages, and in an effort to try to min/max the efficacy of different types of fuel, researchers have long placed an emphasis on a hybrid between solids and liquids - in other words theyâve been working with gels. Liquid fuel, on the other hand, is much more flexible, much like automotive fuel.

While sitting in a tank, they would act like a dense solid, but can also act like a liquid when forced into a combustion chamber. The paper details a new type of fuel that uses an unexpected special ingredient. Lecithin might sound familiar, but not in the context of rocket fuel.

In the context of rocket fuel, lecithin acts simply as an organic gelling agent. When the gel is sitting under normal conditions in a tank, it holds it shape firmly like a gelatin, eliminating the sloshing features that cause so many problems in liquid-fuel rockets. articles.summary: They're main sequence stars like our Sun, meaning they're doing what most people probably think stars do: shining as they fuse hydrogen atoms into helium atoms on a vast scale. But some neutron stars do announce their presence as pulsars .

articles.summary_long:
Most of the stars in the Milky Way are what we might call normal stars. They're main sequence stars like our Sun, meaning they're doing what most people probably think stars do: shining as they fuse hydrogen atoms into helium atoms on a vast scale. They form when massive stars explode as core-collapse supernovae.

Since massive stars are rare, so are neutron stars. But some neutron stars do announce their presence as pulsars . *Somewhere in this globular cluster (NGC 362), a millisecond pulsar and its binary companion, a white dwarf, are in a rare stage of evolution.

The pulsar, which is a dense, rapidly spinning neutron star, has been drawing material away from its less dense white dwarf companion, hastening its evolution into a white dwarf. It's a proto-white dwarf, which indicates that it's only just entering the earliest stages of becoming a white dwarf. This material was likely expelled during the mass-transfer phase, emphasizing how young the white dwarf is.

articles.summary_long:
Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Sometimes Saturn disappears. It doesn't really go away, of course -- it just disappears from our view when Earth's Moon moves in front.

Such a Saturn ian eclipse, more formally called an occultation , was visible in early 2025 along a small swath of Earth -- from Greenland through central Europe and into northern Africa . The featured image is a digital fusion of three images, the first of just Saturn before it disappeared, and then two more of the Moon with different exposure lengths. The images were taken from Sardinia , Italy , after sunset.

The bright dot near Saturn is not a moon of Saturn , but rather the star 85 Aquarii , which is further behind Saturn than Saturn is behind the Moon. The next time the Moon moves in front of Saturn, as visible from some place on Earth , will be in 2031.

So today’s plan purposefully did not have a lot of activities in it so we could get a nice few power positive sols before we get back to drilling. Each of our three sols had a standard morning science block, with an extra exciting brand-new activity on 5061 (more on that shortly!). On 5061, we also conducted a brand-new engineering activity to test parallelism over one of our downlink communications windows.

This is a test of one of those pairs – running our CheMin “Get Data” activity at the same time as we are sending data to one of our orbiters. CheMin Get Data is a high CPU activity which transfers science data from the instrument to our flight computers. Overall, it was an exciting plan full of great remote science as we wait to be able to wrap up our drill campaign.

articles.title: Florestine Perrault Collins Passed for White to Learn the Trade, Then Ran a Black Portrait Studio in New Orleans for Twenty-Nine Years
articles.summary: She got that work by letting her employers assume she was white. She staffed the studio out of her family and her neighborhood.
articles.summary_short: She got that work by letting her employers assume she was white. She staffed the studio out of her family and her neighborhood.
articles.summary_long:
Florestine Perrault was fourteen when she started earning money in photography, hired as a clerk, photo finisher, stationery embosser, and developer by white-owned studios in New Orleans and by the Eastman Kodak Company. She got that work by letting her employers assume she was white. She set up her own studio in the living room of her house on St.

In 1935, six years into the Depression, she moved again, to South Rampart Street, the commercial and cultural spine of Black New Orleans, and renamed the business Collins Studio after her second husband, Herbert Collins. She stayed on South Rampart for the rest of her working life. Counting from the parlor in 1920 to her retirement to Los Angeles in 1949, she ran her own studio for twenty-nine years, through the Depression and a world war, and the addresses tell you she was reading her market carefully the whole time.

She staffed the studio out of her family and her neighborhood. No institution had collected her negatives or her business records, and there was no studio archive to transfer, because nobody had ever treated the studio as an archive. The address where she photographed Black New Orleans for the last fourteen years of her career is a parking lot.

articles.title: Why Your Specialization Doesn’t Start With Camera Skills
articles.summary: Does dividing photographers into portrait, landscape, wedding photographers, and so on really describe professional specialization? Specialization looks like a classification of photographic skills, but in fact it mixes personal traits, working conditions, and accumulated knowledge of the subject.
articles.summary_short: Does dividing photographers into portrait, landscape, wedding photographers, and so on really describe professional specialization? Specialization looks like a classification of photographic skills, but in fact it mixes personal traits, working conditions, and accumulated knowledge of the subject.
articles.summary_long:
Does dividing photographers into portrait, landscape, wedding photographers, and so on really describe professional specialization? Specialization looks like a classification of photographic skills, but in fact it mixes personal traits, working conditions, and accumulated knowledge of the subject. The subject determines the area they work in.

A person does not become suited to working with people because they chose portrait photography. They end up in portrait photography and stay there because they are able to work with people. Sports photography does not make a photographer fast or resistant to pressure; a person with these qualities is able to work in sports photography for years.

What, then, do ten years in one specialization mean? Ten years in certain working conditions and around a certain subject. They are better prepared to work with a certain subject and under certain conditions.

articles.summary_long:
Son Lux ’s newest music video is an atmospheric mini-epic. Last month, the video premiered at MASS MoCA —the piece is a joint commission by the museum and Pioneer Works and made in collaboration with Alex Cook —as an immersive, 17-minute installation titled “Out Into Us (Slow Down),” complementing the release of the band’s ninth studio album. “In the last decade, social media has created a reality in which music is often eclipsed by visuals, served up in an endless buffet of bite-sized and contextless flavors,” says a statement.

Portraying a multigenerational family seated around a table and passing the time in one another’s company, the video transports us back at least a century as scenes of a giant dust cloud evoke the Dust Bowl. Cook conjures tension, atmosphere, and moments of disrupted reality in a slippage of past and present. The Dust Bowl itself was inherently linked to an intense period when homesteaders, dreaming of prosperous lives for themselves, plowed vast swaths of prairie for their farms.

These bucolic tableaux and their romantic ideals could even be said to have functioned something like social media does today, as a way to spread information. “Sound can create a sanctuary—a space in which we can remember what it feels like to be present in our bodies and lost in our thoughts,” says the band’s guitarist, Rafiq Bhatia. “When you decrease the playback speed of a piece of music, you can really linger in its hidden corners and shadows: passing tensions and moments of release become whole rooms you can step into and stay for a while.”

articles.title: Caribbean Surrealism and Ancestral Memory Merge in Kelly Sinnapah Mary’s Lush Portraits
articles.summary: Tattooed with verdant foliage, the central figure in Kelly Sinnapah Mary ’s portraits is both a product of and subsumed by the plant life that surrounds her. Born in the French Caribbean territory of Guadeloupe, the artist conjures the mythic stories of her home through surreal scenes in which humans, flora, and fauna find a sort of hybrid harmony.
articles.summary_short: Tattooed with verdant foliage, the central figure in Kelly Sinnapah Mary ’s portraits is both a product of and subsumed by the plant life that surrounds her. articles.summary_long:
Tattooed with verdant foliage, the central figure in Kelly Sinnapah Mary ’s portraits is both a product of and subsumed by the plant life that surrounds her. Born in the French Caribbean territory of Guadeloupe, the artist conjures the mythic stories of her home through surreal scenes in which humans, flora, and fauna find a sort of hybrid harmony. Sinnapah Mary’s recurring figure is named Sanbras, which the artist derived from a derogatory children’s book popular in the 19th and 20th centuries.

Through uncanny compositions that rely heavily on saturated color and delicate, organic textures, Sanbras appears as a subversive figure who morphs across various bodies of work and nods to the artist’s enduring questions: how relationships between all living beings manifest and the ways political forces—European colonialism and anthropocentrism, in particular—shape such connections. Melding various forms of knowledge and cultural symbols is a central part of Sinnapah Mary’s work, which emerges from her own evolving understanding of her family history. How a familial history informs one’s understanding of place and identity appears in the tender portraits of The Book of Violette , which is named after artist’s grandmother.

Often centering on lone protagonists, this series unfolds through folklore and references to the ways ancestral memory is passed through generations. Sinnapah Mary has described her grandmother’s magical garden of medicinal plants, for example, which appears as luscious flowers with human heads sprout from a plaid coverlet in “Violette’s Garden: My Father’s Shoes.” Holding a book with gilded pages and smoking a pipe, the schoolgirl stares at the viewer with a third eye, a symbol of wisdom and spiritual connection in Hinduism. Save the date for Sinnapah Mary’s Between earth and sea opening in February at The Aldrich Contemporary Art Museum in Ridgefield, Connecticut.

articles.title: Amy Liu Explores Light and Dark through Glitz, Mystique, and Opera
articles.summary: Not unlike the way a pearl grows inside a mollusk, wherein an irritant or parasite is gradually coated in a mineral called nacre, Amy Liu ’s paintings comprise layers of oil pigment over underpaintings. This preparation technique dates to the early Renaissance, its first use attributed to Jan van Eyck, who added a monochrome glaze to the surface of panels to establish tonal values before building up the picture.

articles.summary_long:
Not unlike the way a pearl grows inside a mollusk, wherein an irritant or parasite is gradually coated in a mineral called nacre, Amy Liu ’s paintings comprise layers of oil pigment over underpaintings. This preparation technique dates to the early Renaissance, its first use attributed to Jan van Eyck, who added a monochrome glaze to the surface of panels to establish tonal values before building up the picture. In her solo exhibition Pearled Chiaroscuro at Harper’s , Liu taps into the Renaissance in more ways than one.

Liu focuses on women wearing embellished gowns and draped in elaborate jewelry, with an emphasis on pearls. She also invokes the spirit of a night at opera, drawing on her own background as a trained soprano. Rather than highlighting the identities of the figures, whether performers or spectators, the artist focuses on their elaborate and luxurious garments.

By concealing the women’s identities and viewing them through their sartorial choices, Liu explores how high fashion is a channel of not only status but one’s sense of self, where in turn, the garments literally and figuratively mask the person wearing them. “Figures are abstracted and their identities deliberately concealed, as if supporting the ornamentation rather than the other way around,” the gallery says. Pearled Chiaroscuro continues through December 19 at Harper’s Apartment on the Upper East Side, New York City.

articles.summary_long:
Le projet de loi Résilience est examiné en séance publique après plusieurs reports. Son adoption doit permettre de préciser le cadre réglementaire applicable aux milliers d’organisations concernées. Le projet de loi Résilience est examiné à l’Assemblée nationale du 9 au 13 novembre.

Présenté en Conseil des ministres le 15 octobre 2024, le projet de loi relatif à la résilience des infrastructures critiques et au renforcement de la cybersécurité a été adopté par le Sénat en mars 2025, puis à l’unanimité par la commission spéciale de l’Assemblée nationale en septembre de la même année. Le nombre de secteurs couverts passe de 6 à 18, et celui des organisations concernées de quelques centaines à près de 15 000, réparties entre entités essentielles et entités importantes. Les entités essentielles s’exposent à des amendes pouvant atteindre 10 M€ ou 2 % de leur chiffre d’affaires annuel mondial.

Pour les entités importantes, le plafond est fixé à 7 M€ ou 1,4 % du chiffre d’affaires mondial. Cette disposition oppose deux approches de la sécurité. Anne Le Hénanff, ministre déléguée chargée de l’Intelligence artificielle et du Numérique, le considère comme un cavalier législatif, autrement dit une disposition sans lien suffisamment direct avec l’objet du projet de loi.

Réunis à Munich le 9 novembre, ils ont mis en avant l’expérience du continent dans l’automobile et les technologies industrielles, rapporte Reuters . « Pour moi, l’IA industrielle ou IA physique est avant tout un enjeu que l’Europe se doit de remporter », a déclaré Jochen Hanebeck, directeur général d’Infineon. Selon ces dirigeants, l’arrivée de l’IA dans les véhicules, les robots et les machines industrielles soutiendra la demande de composants fiables.

Jean-Marc Chéry, directeur général de STMicroelectronics, souligne la nécessité de rapprocher fabricants et clients, notamment pour entraîner les robots dans des environnements simulés. Pour Rafael Sotomayor, directeur général de NXP, les compétences historiques européennes constituent un avantage dans la conception de systèmes sûrs. Les 85 M€ restants financeront l’infrastructure cloud de la plateforme, les services d’accompagnement et le développement d’outils de conception open source. Pour Bruxelles, renforcer les capacités européennes de conception est indispensable pour offrir davantage de débouchés aux infrastructures de production installées sur le continent. La Commission européenne considère que le développement d’un écosystème de concepteurs locaux créera une demande supplémentaire pour les capacités industrielles européennes.

L’objectif initial était notamment de porter à 20 % d’ici à 2030 la part de l’Union européenne dans la production mondiale de puces. La European Chip Design Platform sera opérée par un consortium conduit par l’institut belge de recherche imec, avec le soutien de l’entreprise commune européenne consacrée aux semi-conducteurs (Chips Joint Undertaking). Le réseau européen de centres de compétences dans les semi-conducteurs doit également aider à orienter les entreprises vers les dispositifs de soutien disponibles.

articles.title: Nearby Dwarf Galaxies Show Surprising Lack Of Oxygen, Says Paper
articles.summary: We found that typically 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars in these low-mass galaxies is still found inside those galaxies today: mostly in their gas, but small fractions are also in the stars and dust, says Telford. Similar measurements of oxygen (and other heavy elements) lost from galaxies have been made for massive galaxies like the Milky Way, says Telford.
articles.summary_short: We found that typically 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars in these low-mass galaxies is still found inside those galaxies today: mostly in their gas, but small fractions are also in the stars and dust, says Telford. Similar measurements of oxygen (and other heavy elements) lost from galaxies have been made for massive galaxies like the Milky Way, says Telford.
articles.summary_long:
Vital to almost all life as we know it, oxygen has long been valued as a tracer of the chemical evolution of the of the cosmos. As such, it provides a practical means of tracing how the heavy elements of iron, carbon, nickel, magnesium and sulfur --- the real building blocks of habitable planets like our own --- are distributed throughout the galaxy and beyond. For the first time, we have measured both how much oxygen produced by stars in low-mass galaxies remains in those galaxies, and how much oxygen has been lost from those galaxies throughout their lifetimes, Grace Telford, the paperâs second author and an assistant professor at the University of Utahâs Dept.

The findings show that dwarf galaxies can hold onto only a small fraction of the oxygen made by stars, says NASA. We found that typically 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars in these low-mass galaxies is still found inside those galaxies today: mostly in their gas, but small fractions are also in the stars and dust, says Telford. The explanation is that energetic radiation from massive stars and their deaths as supernovae drive oxygen-rich gas out of the galaxies over time, she says.

Similar measurements of oxygen (and other heavy elements) lost from galaxies have been made for massive galaxies like the Milky Way, says Telford. In low-mass galaxies like those in the GLOW project, that value is more like one oxygen atom for every 10,000-20,000 hydrogen atoms, she says. The GLOW project found that low-mass galaxies lose more oxygen than current galaxy formation simulations predict, implying that we donât yet have a complete understanding of how massive stars interact with their host galaxies, says Telford.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 9 – Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula

articles.summary_long:
Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: Does the blue nebula look like the head of a witch? The nebula is known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula because, it is said, the nebula's shape resembles a Halloween-style caricature of a witch's head.

Exactly how, though, can be a topic of imaginative speculation . What is clear is that IC 2118 is about 50 light-years across and made of gas and dust that points to -- because it has been partly eroded by -- the nearby star Rigel . One of the brighter stars in the constellation Orion, Rigel lies just below the center of the featured image .

The blue color of the Witch Head Nebula and is caused not only by Rigel's intense blue starlight but also because the dust grains scatter blue light more efficiently than red. The same physical process causes Earth's daytime sky to appear blue , although the scatterers in planet Earth's atmosphere are molecules of nitrogen and oxygen .

This story is an update to the Antarctic ozone hole feature in our World of Change series , which documents how Earth changes over months, seasons, and years. NASA satellite instruments revealed the continental scale of this Antarctic ozone thinning, and it came to be known as the ozone hole.

Red and yellow areas indicate the ozone hole. These maps show the state of the ozone hole each year on the day of maximum depth—the day the lowest ozone concentrations were measured. The deepest ozone hole occurred in 1994, when concentrations fell to just 73 DU on September 30.

In the early years of the 21st century, annual ozone holes roughly stabilized (see NASA Ozone Watch for annual averages). Human-produced bromine compounds, which are far less abundant but much more destructive to ozone, also contribute to the Antarctic ozone hole. NASA Earth Observatory images by Lauren Dauphin, using data from NASA Ozone Watch .

articles.title: 7 Everyday Habits That Quietly Damage Your Camera Gear
articles.summary: A shattered filter or a scratched front element rarely comes from a dramatic fall off a cliff, and more often traces back to a loose ball head, a lens swap in the wind, or a tripod slung over your shoulder on the walk to the next spot. Those small habits stack up over years of shooting, and changing them costs far less than replacing glass.
articles.summary_short: A shattered filter or a scratched front element rarely comes from a dramatic fall off a cliff, and more often traces back to a loose ball head, a lens swap in the wind, or a tripod slung over your shoulder on the walk to the next spot. articles.summary_long:
A shattered filter or a scratched front element rarely comes from a dramatic fall off a cliff, and more often traces back to a loose ball head, a lens swap in the wind, or a tripod slung over your shoulder on the walk to the next spot. Those small habits stack up over years of shooting, and changing them costs far less than replacing glass. The first is carrying the camera mounted on the tripod, legs extended, over your shoulder.

Put the hood on, flip the rig so the lens points down, and use an L-bracket or a plate with anti-rotation pins, since a single-screw plate lets the camera spin and swing the lens into a leg or a rock. His approach is to seal the camera in a Ziploc bag before the transition, then let it warm up inside the bag before taking it out. Carry a camera from 20°F air into a heated cabin, and the moisture in the indoor air condenses on the cold body and inside the lens.

The bag trick works in both directions, as long as you seal the camera in the air it's currently sitting in before you change environments. Weather sealing, he points out, isn't waterproofing, and no shot is worth leaving an uncovered camera on a tripod in a shower. Most of his own mishaps happened that way, from lens hoods dropped off cliffs to lens caps dropped in the water.

articles.title: The Story of One of the Most Famous Photos Ever
articles.summary: The film in the back was Fujichrome Velvia, an ISO 50 transparency stock. What O'Rear defends is the transparency, not the bitmap Microsoft shipped.
articles.summary_short: The film in the back was Fujichrome Velvia, an ISO 50 transparency stock. What O'Rear defends is the transparency, not the bitmap Microsoft shipped.
articles.summary_long:
In January 1996, Charles O'Rear pulled onto the shoulder of California State Route 121 in southern Sonoma County, pushed a Mamiya RZ67 through a wire fence, and made a few exposures of a bare green hill. The film in the back was Fujichrome Velvia, an ISO 50 transparency stock. Two years later, that frame was sitting on a Corbis stock catalog disc as image 71810, with a copyright bar across the bottom reading "©CHARLES O'REAR/Westlight 71810WL." The popular version puts the picture in Napa Valley.

The hill O'Rear photographed had been cleared years earlier for the same reason. In a 2010 interview, he measured his frame against Ansel Adams. CNET wrote in 2014 that Microsoft cropped the picture and pumped up the green, and the Napa Valley Register wrote the same year that Microsoft had admitted to darkening the green hill.

What O'Rear defends is the transparency, not the bitmap Microsoft shipped. Same clouds, same hill, same wispy cirrus in the upper left, nothing moved. In 2000, the XP team reached O'Rear through Corbis, and they did not want a license.

Madison Huang, fille de Jensen Huang et cadre de Nvidia, a annulé une visite prévue à Séoul à l’occasion d’un événement consacré à l’intelligence artificielle. Rebellions a attribué ces annulations à des circonstances internes inévitables chez Nvidia. Selon lui, un changement à la tête de Nvidia modifierait en revanche complètement la donne.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Explanation: The sky glows with soft pinkish colors of fading twilight in this serendipitous mountaintop vista. Taken in subfreezing temperatures, the thoughtfully composed photo shows snowy, rugged peaks seen from a mountain pass on 2017 November 14.

Below lies the village of La Villa, Alta Badia in Italy 's Dolomite Alps . Above the nestled village lights, the constellation Ursa Major hangs over the northern horizon. But most stunning is the intense fireball meteor.

It was captured during the camera's exposure by chance as it flashed east to west across the northern horizon, under Ursa Major's familiar Big Dipper asterism . Sightings of this major fireball meteor were widely reported in European skies, making it one of the most reported fireball events ever for planet Earth's American Meteor Society and the International Meteor Organization . The meteor's measured track over Germany is consistent with its origin near the active radiant of November's Northern Taurid Meteor Shower , a shower associated with dust from Encke's comet .

articles.title: The 3 Camera Modes One Wedding Photographer Uses for Every Portrait
articles.summary: After roughly 400 weddings, Martin Castein has narrowed his portrait work down to three modes: full manual, manual with auto ISO, and aperture priority paired with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed. Aperture priority with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed flips the logic, letting the camera hold base ISO and push the shutter faster as the light gets brighter.
articles.summary_short: After roughly 400 weddings, Martin Castein has narrowed his portrait work down to three modes: full manual, manual with auto ISO, and aperture priority paired with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed. Aperture priority with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed flips the logic, letting the camera hold base ISO and push the shutter faster as the light gets brighter.
articles.summary_long:
Manual mode has a reputation as the serious way to shoot portraits, and plenty of people switch to it the moment they feel comfortable with their camera. Outdoors, with clouds drifting across the sun and subjects walking in and out of shade, that habit can leave you chasing exposure instead of watching your subject. After roughly 400 weddings, Martin Castein has narrowed his portrait work down to three modes: full manual, manual with auto ISO, and aperture priority paired with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed.

The mode choice rests on a simple idea he lays out early: "ISO gives you headroom in low light, and shutter speed gives you headroom in bright light." On a sunny day, your ISO is probably already sitting between 100 and 400, close to the floor, so it has nowhere left to go. That's where manual with auto ISO falls apart in daylight: at f/1.2 or f/1.4, the camera slams into ISO 100, the image starts blowing out, and you're back to turning the shutter dial yourself. Aperture priority with auto ISO and a minimum shutter speed flips the logic, letting the camera hold base ISO and push the shutter faster as the light gets brighter.

Castein skips the auto setting because shutter speed, more than aperture or ISO, decides whether he gets the picture at all, and he treats in-body stabilization as if it isn't there, since it steadies the camera and does nothing for a subject who moves. Under 1/125 s, he takes a lot more, and slower than that, he asks people to hold still or, in his words, to "move in slow motion." The setting pays off in noise, too: at an outdoor cafe in open shade, a 1/1,000 s minimum had his ISO at 3,200, and because his subjects were sitting still, lowering it to 1/500 s brought the ISO straight down to 1,600. Night is when he goes back to manual with auto ISO, since ISO has the headroom in the dark, and he warns that many cameras will drop below your minimum shutter speed once auto ISO hits its limit.

Once focus is separated from the shutter button, you can set it on the background, release, and the camera won't refocus on your subject when you half-press to shoot. articles.title: Abstract Wool Compositions Cascade from Weathered Metal in Amine El Gotaibi’s Sculptures
articles.summary: It moves freely across territories, indifferent to the categories that divide them,” Amine El Gotaibi says. The Moroccan artist positions nature’s apathy toward national boundaries as an entry point for unraveling the forces that shape our perceptions and memories of a place.
articles.summary_short: It moves freely across territories, indifferent to the categories that divide them,” Amine El Gotaibi says. The Moroccan artist positions nature’s apathy toward national boundaries as an entry point for unraveling the forces that shape our perceptions and memories of a place.
articles.summary_long:
It moves freely across territories, indifferent to the categories that divide them,” Amine El Gotaibi says. The Moroccan artist positions nature’s apathy toward national boundaries as an entry point for unraveling the forces that shape our perceptions and memories of a place. El Gotaibi’s most recent body of work is on view this month at Southern Guild .

Presented in an exhibition titled Wind From the North , a suite of sculptures made of metal and wool speak to the tensions between the land and the state and the ways we mark change. Affixed to these aged backdrops are tufts of beige and rust-colored fibers, which are either wound into tightly knotted tufts or left free-flowing. Echoing the undulating terrain of mountains and the countryside, the cascading fibers tether to the artist’s interest in examining the landscapes of his home country and Northern Africa, more broadly.

For El Gotaibi, this material significance directly links to his desire to challenge the idea that Africa’s cultural contributions are most likely to emerge from the central and south. Instead, Wind from the North , an exhibition statement says, “extends this proposition beyond fixed coordinates, imagining geography as porous and interconnected, shaped as much by what passes through it as by the lines drawn around it.” Wind From the North is on view through January 9 in New York. Find more from El Gotaibi on Instagram .

articles.title: What Else Could It Mean? A Book Surveys the Playful, Iconoclastic Works of James Wines
articles.summary: An unparalleled devotee of wit and play, Wines is behind SITE (Sculpture in the Environment), a New York-based studio founded in 1970 with a portfolio that spans commercial construction, urban infrastructure, public art, and more. Published by Skira, What Else Could It Mean?
articles.summary_short: An unparalleled devotee of wit and play, Wines is behind SITE (Sculpture in the Environment), a New York-based studio founded in 1970 with a portfolio that spans commercial construction, urban infrastructure, public art, and more. Published by Skira, What Else Could It Mean?
articles.summary_long:
It’s not uncommon for artists and architects to espouse a desire for breaking conventions and pushing boundaries, but so few have embodied such a mandate as James Wines. An unparalleled devotee of wit and play, Wines is behind SITE (Sculpture in the Environment), a New York-based studio founded in 1970 with a portfolio that spans commercial construction, urban infrastructure, public art, and more. No matter the project, SITE’s approach is rooted in questioning the division between art and architecture and defying expectations.

In the preface to the new book, What Else Could It Mean? , Wines describes how he spent months in Rome after college soaking in the religious designs and civically unified architecture, which inspired what became his signature mode of working. “What else could it mean?” became a driving ethos that centered around “architecture as a critique of itself, as an inversion of design expectations, as humorous insights and the absorption of context as a motivating source of ideas,” he writes.

Published by Skira, What Else Could It Mean? showcases dozens of projects from the SITE oeuvre. The BEST designs are just a piece of SITE’s broader commentary on commercialization.

Le 4 novembre 2026, Qualcomm a annoncé avoir été retenu pour fournir les technologies qui équiperont le futur réseau terrestre 5G de Starlink Mobile aux Etats-Unis.

Pour cette infrastructure, SpaceX s'appuiera sur deux plateformes de Qualcomm Technologies, Dragonwing QRU100 et QDU100. Qualcomm met également en avant les gains attendus en matière de couverture, de capacité et d'efficacité énergétique. Selon Qualcomm, cette approche doit notamment contribuer à augmenter les capacités du réseau tout en maîtrisant la consommation énergétique des équipements.

Qualcomm fournira les composants et les logiciels nécessaires au traitement radio et à la couche physique. SpaceX conservera de son côté la maîtrise des autres éléments de l'architecture réseau, notamment les couches logicielles supérieures. Le contrat porte néanmoins, à ce stade, sur le déploiement d'un réseau terrestre 5G.

articles.title: Interstellar Visitor 3I/ATLAS Shows Water Ice Behaves the Same Across Alien Star Systems
articles.summary: Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. But thereâs still plenty left to understand about our most recent interstellar visitor.
articles.summary_short: Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. But thereâs still plenty left to understand about our most recent interstellar visitor.
articles.summary_long:
Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. And it just so happens that in the intervening years between the last known interstellar visitor (2I/Borisov in 2019), we got a major upgrade in our observational capabilities with the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Typically, water ice is pretty easy to spot for astronomers.

In fact, JWST observed this interstellar visitor at three different times during its journey through our solar system, starting when it was about 3.31 astronomical units (AU) out from perihelion all the way through when it was about 5.65 AU past perihelion. After perihelion, the grains of ice and dust appeared to include a second population of larger, micron-sized, ice-rich aggregates. The infrared patterns of 3I/ATLAS match certain types of Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs) in our own solar system.

After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth's atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia .

The featured image is a mosaic created in 2018 using the first one million images captured by the satellite's Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope . Swift had a combination of instruments, including an X-ray telescope and a gamma-ray telescope , that worked together to enable humanity to study, in unprecedented detail, the fastest and most energetic explosions in the universe. The most recent solar maximum accelerated the decay of the satellite's orbit.

An innovative mission to rescue Swift by boosting its orbit was not successful . Swift burned on reentry like a shooting star, but the impressive data acquired by the telescope over its mission will continue to bring light to the mysteries of the cosmos for years to come. May it keep inspiring new missions to boldly go into space, explore new data and seek out new science.

Dévoilé cet été, le thème de cette 17e édition tient en un mot : « Surprise » . Il succède à « La beauté » , qui avait porté l’édition 2026 à un record de 3 255 films (2 577 courts-métrages et 113 mini-séries de six épisodes), dont 42 % réalisés par des femmes, avant un Grand Prix du Jury remis à L’Éclat de Tansi Makele.

Deux formats sont proposés : un ou plusieurs courts-métrages de 2 min 20, ou une mini-série de six épisodes de 2 min 20 reliés par un fil narratif. Annoncé en septembre, le firmware 2.00 de la Nikon ZR a été détaillé par Nikon le 3 novembre. Au programme : le Log3G10 en H.265 , un réglage de la réduction du bruit, le focus peaking en R3D NE et plus de personnalisation. La v2.00 va plus loin, et Nikon la présente comme la première mise à jour majeure de la caméra.

En Log3G10 comme en N-Log, on peut choisir parmi quatre niveaux de réduction du bruit en haute sensibilité. Côté mise au point, le focus peaking arrive enfin en R3D NE, y compris quand un LUT 3D est appliqué. Nikon n’annonce en revanche aucune évolution de l’autofocus avec cette version.

En septembre, Nikon avait aussi indiqué que RED mettait à jour ses applications de pilotage à distance RED Control et RED Control Pro pour les rendre compatibles avec la ZR. Nikon annonce que le firmware 2.00 sortira avant la fin de 2026 , sans date précise pour l’instant. Contrairement aux drones à suivi automatique de DJI, Beni ne vole pas : il roule au sol, aux côtés de son sujet. articles.title: OpenAI dévoile GPT-6 Cyber

articles.summary_short: Spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et réservé à un cercle restreint de clients, GPT-6 Cyber vise à faciliter la détection et l'analyse des vulnérabilités logicielles. OpenAI revendique notamment la découverte de 81 failles inédites de haute gravité dans Firefox.
articles.summary_long:
Spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et réservé à un cercle restreint de clients, GPT-6 Cyber vise à faciliter la détection et l'analyse des vulnérabilités logicielles. OpenAI revendique notamment la découverte de 81 failles inédites de haute gravité dans Firefox. Quelques jours après avoir dévoilé Image 2.6, la nouvelle version de son générateur d'images, OpenAI annonce GPT-6 Cyber, un modèle spécialisé dans la cybersécurité et dérivé de GPT-6 Astra.

OpenAI poursuit le développement de ses capacités en cybersécurité avec GPT-6 Cyber, une déclinaison spécialisée de son modèle GPT-6 Astra. Les premiers résultats communiqués par OpenAI illustrent les capacités du modèle. Lors de travaux menés sur Firefox, GPT-6 Cyber a permis d’identifier 81 vulnérabilités inédites, classées de haute gravité par Mozilla.

Le modèle aurait permis de reproduire 1 724 vulnérabilités et de développer 948 exploits fonctionnels. OpenAI classe ce modèle au niveau « critique » en matière de cybersécurité, une première pour ses modèles Cyber. GPT-6 Cyber n’est donc pas proposé en accès libre.

The dramatic illumination reveals the plumes that continuously spew into space from the south pole of Saturn's 500 kilometer diameter moon .

Discovered by Cassini in 2005, the icy plumes are likely connected to an ocean beneath the ice shell of Enceladus. They supply material directly to Saturn's outer, tenuous E ring and make the surface of Enceladus as reflective as snow. Across the scene, Saturn's icy rings scatter sunlight toward Cassini's cameras.

Beyond the rings (lower right), the night side of 80 kilometer diameter moon Pandora is faintly lit by Saturnlight .

The third-largest island in the Mediterranean Sea exposes an ancient piece of the ocean floor and hosts a clowder of cats. The island of Cyprus began to form some 90 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous , with molten rock pouring from the seafloor, solidifying, and building new oceanic crust . Remnants of that ancient island are still visible in the dark rocks of the Troodos Mountains .

During the Miocene , considerably younger layers of chalk, limestone, marl, and other marine sedimentary rocks accumulated around the island, providing material that developed into a second, smaller island to the south during a later period of geologic uplift . The cape today is still home to the Holy Monastery of St. Nicholas of the Cats , a place where legend says that monks encouraged newly arrived Egyptian cats to hunt snakes.

“For decades, NASA Aeronautics has used X-planes to develop technologies that advance aviation,” said Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. The flight took place at Rogers Dry Lake near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.

During the tests, the SPLICE payload used an advanced guidance system to map the terrain and assess potential landing areas. If the system determines the targeted landing area is unsafe, the system diverts the drone to a safer location. “This flight test is the culmination of almost a decade of work, for the SPLICE project,” said Davis Adams, NASA project manager.

Validation of the guidance and navigation systems are applicable to terrestrial, lunar, and Martian descent and landing missions.” NASA has worked with a number of commercial lunar lander providers to implement iterations of SPLICE into their platforms. “Some of the companies also are evaluating the system’s navigation capabilities for precision landing applications, as well as potential extensions for autonomous surface mobility.” NASA’s Flight Opportunities project, based at NASA Armstrong, enabled flight testing of the SPLICE project early in its development that laid a foundation for it to continue advancing its technology readiness level to what it is today. Flight testing included both a descent altitude and a landing trajectory in 2019 similar to what is expected on a lunar mission and the demonstration of two NASA-developed precision landing sensor systems in 2020.

Kodachrome died when one small lab in southeast Kansas went quiet, because a Kodachrome roll was not a color film in any sense a modern photographer would recognize.

Nearly every other color film you have shot carries its couplers inside the emulsion, waiting for oxidized developer to meet them and form dye in place. The yellow developer then builds yellow dye in the top layer. The middle green-sensitive layer gets no light at all.

The film only becomes a color film at the end of that chain, and the chain was scrapped in Parsons in January 2011. You can still find frozen Kodachrome on auction sites, and you can still shoot it. The one machine it cannot run is the one that made Kodachrome a color film, and there are 50,000 slides of trains in Arkansas that exist because one man got them to Kansas in time.

articles.summary_long:
Shoot a flash portrait at f/1.2 in midday sun and you run into a wall fast: most cameras stop syncing with a flash somewhere around 1/160 to 1/250 s, and anything faster leaves dark bands across the frame. Sony's a9 III and its global shutter offer a way past that wall, which puts high-speed sync, the usual workaround, in an interesting spot. The high-speed sync shots come from a Sony a7R VI with the Sony FE 50mm f/1.2 GM , because the Sony a9 III won't go into high-speed sync mode at all.

At f/1.2, the ceiling drops to 1/16,000 s, which is still far beyond what a focal plane shutter can sync at. For high-speed sync, the flash sat at 5.2. The logic carries over to leaf shutter cameras such as the Fujifilm X100VI , where the flash also fires as one burst at shutter speeds a focal plane shutter can't sync at.

On any camera, shutter speed sets how bright the background looks, and the flash sets how bright your subject looks. A global or leaf shutter lets you push those two apart much further. What the global shutter opens up for portraits is control over ambient light.

articles.title: Assyria is Far from Ancient in Esther Elia’s Characterizations of Contemporary ‘Diasporic Deities’
articles.summary: Across ancient Mesopotamia, lamassu figures assumed the form of a winged goddess. She adds: The home is where our language is spoken.
articles.summary_short: Across ancient Mesopotamia, lamassu figures assumed the form of a winged goddess. She adds: The home is where our language is spoken.
articles.summary_long:
Across ancient Mesopotamia, lamassu figures assumed the form of a winged goddess. In the ancient Assyrian Empire, giant bulls or lions with human heads and wings represented the deities, which artisans often carved at a monumental scale to protect cities and palaces. For Albuquerque-based Esther Elia , who is of Assyrian and Irish descent, lamassu are anything but a relic of the distant past.

Through sculpture, paintings, and textiles, the artist explores contemporary Assyrian experience through pattern, fashion, and autobiography. Her solo exhibition, Bazaar Ashuraya at Hecho a Mano , centers around a new collection of acrylic paintings, plus tile mosaics and functional objects. Elia delves into the theme of home, where lamps, garments, and paintings evocative of rugs or tapestries portray vibrant figures, shapes, and objects associated with daily life.

“The home is where Assyria lives and breathes,” Elia says in a statement. She adds: The home is where our language is spoken. Even if we speak English or Arabic or Farsi or French or Swedish outside of the home, the home is where Assyrian food is made, where Assyrian customs thrive, and where culture is maintained as well as created—pushed forward.

Raised in Nigeria’s Kaduna region, Obijiaku recently moved to Chicago, where he has grappled with the emotional resonance of distance and getting used to an entirely new place.

“Seen through a sentimental lens, these settings lend the paintings an intimate, dreamlike quality, as though recalling a presence from memory,” says a statement from Roberts Projects , which will be presenting the artist’s forthcoming solo show, Wherever You Are, Remember Me . Obijiaku relishes how everyday experiences have the potential to prompt memories. Sounds can transport us to specific times and places in our past.

articles.summary_long:
Après une première série de piratages en France en octobre, les systèmes de réfrigération de plusieurs enseignes européennes ont de nouveau été ciblés ce 2 novembre. Belgique, Suède, Irlande et plusieurs autres pays sont concernés. Lundi 2 novembre, les installations frigorifiques de plusieurs supermarchés européens ont été manipulées à distance, provoquant des pertes de marchandises et des perturbations opérationnelles.

Plusieurs enseignes européennes ont signalé des dysfonctionnements de leurs équipements de réfrigération. En Belgique, une quarantaine de magasins Delhaize auraient été touchés, tandis que plusieurs points de vente Carrefour ont également signalé des incidents. Des magasins Intermarché et Spar figurent aussi parmi les établissements concernés.

La Suède et l'Irlande sont également affectées, l'enseigne ICA a confirmé des incidents dans plusieurs magasins, tandis qu'au moins treize supermarchés SuperValu ont confirmé la perte de produits frais et surgelés. Le Luxembourg, les Pays-Bas et l'Estonie figurent aussi parmi les pays concernés. Environ 700 magasins auraient été concernés par la compromission de leurs systèmes de réfrigération.
